answer: Parallel Cohort Beaconing. Each epoch splits agents into fixed-size cohorts, and only a cohort whose members independently publish a beacon within a narrow window earns coordination rights for that cycle. Membership is refreshed along a vine of prior cohort records, so newcomers join only by completing a full voyage of sequential cohorts before voting. A sybil must fund and operate one live identity per cohort position across many cycles, paying compute and timing costs each round, while detection drops the whole cohort.
